title: Spectral token-flow lighthouse for windowed PR regression detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a lightweight but robust PR-time sentinel that detects temporal regressions in tokens/sec and p95 using spectral / distributional comparisons over short rolling windows. Unlike a single-point p95 check, this ticket implements a token-flow spectrogram approach that captures burstiness, warmup behavior, and steady-state throughput shifts. The sentinel will run in PR CI (fast smoke harness) and produce human-readable diagnostics and an artifact (spectrogram + divergence metrics) to help triage. Key design constraints: runnable within PR time budgets (~10-15m), deterministic across CI runners, and resilient to noise from VM cold starts and ephemeral infra variability.
acceptance_criteria: A lightweight CI job that synthesizes or replays a 60s windowed workload and emits a token-flow spectrogram artifact
Automated calculation of distributional drift metrics (KL/JS divergence and a moving-drift-test score) comparing PR run to pinned baseline version
Gate boolean: job exits non-zero when drift score exceeds adaptive threshold tuned per-model and per-context-length
Per-model context-length stratification is supported (8/64/2048) and thresholds are configurable via repo-level config
Artifacts (PNG spectrogram, CSV token-rate time series, JSON metrics) are uploaded to CI artifacts and a perf-dashboard link is included in PR checks
False-positive rate on historical samples < 2% and true-positive detection of injected 10% throughput regressions in synthetic tests
comments: 2026-01-12 Maya Chen: Initial triage. Proposed 'spectral token-flow' concept after reviewing flaky p95 gates in last quarter. Scoped to PR smoke job + dashboard artifact. Recommended dependencies ENG-24680 for waveform detector baseline and ENG-62411 for slice stratification logic.

2026-01-18 Diego Rivera: Spike complete. Implemented proof-of-concept that converts token timestamps to a short-time Fourier transform-like spectrogram using overlapping windows. Early results show clearer separation for burst regressions vs steady drifts compared to single p95 values. Saved artifacts to gs://redwood-perf-spikes/eng-999451/.

2026-01-22 PM review (Aisha Patel): PM suggests adding contextual labels (model, seq_len, quantization profile) to artifacts and defaulting thresholds to conservative values for customer-facing models. Also requested integration with existing perf-dashboard (dashboard/perf-regression).

2026-01-26 Design feedback (Liam O'Connor): Requested human-readable summary in checks UI with 3 colored states (OK / Warning / Failing) and a link to spectrogram + 'explainability' bullets (peak burst time, median tokens/sec drop, warmup deviation).

2026-01-30 Diego Rivera: Prototype gate added to PR runner (non-blocking by default). Observed two intermittent false positives traced to CI cold-start artifacts; added VM-warmup detection and a 5s discard window at job start.

2026-02-03 Maya Chen: Experiment results uploaded. Injected synthetic 12% throughput regression detected consistently across 10 runs.
